title: NDSU student group plans protest against campus rape culture in Fargo
seoTitle: Fargo protest against campus rape culture

tea.why: Organisers and students are frustrated with campus rape culture and how victims of sexual assault are treated.
tea.want: To end campus rape culture and support victims of sexual assault.
tea.changed: Oct 25: Organisers announced upcoming sign-making sessions ahead of the Nov. 1 protest.

summary: Members of a student organization at North Dakota State University plan to hold an "End Rape Culture" protest and solidarity demonstration at Churchill Field in Fargo. Hosted by the Women’s Activist Organization, the event invites students from NDSU, Concordia College, and Minnesota State University Moorhead, along with community members. According to the organization's president, the protest was inspired by a recent civil lawsuit concerning allegations of a gang rape at Cornell University. Organisers stated that the demonstration aims to express students' frustrations regarding how sexual assault is handled and to support survivors. No official response from university or police authorities regarding the planned protest was reported in the sources.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: The Women’s Activist Organization announced plans for an End Rape Culture protest at Churchill Field.
Organisers detailed that students from multiple local colleges and community members are invited to the solidarity demonstration.
